source: Hi. Make An FPS Shooter Game With A Loading GUI. Once Loaded On The Main Hub Screen, Have A Button Where It Says Play An When Clicking It. it Loads You Onto The Map\n\nMake The Map First. the Map Style Will Be Like The Hood But A Bit Different.

answers.ask: What mode is this - team deathmatch, free-for-all, or an objective?
answers.answer: Make it free-for-all so players spawn into the map and fight each other.

answers.ask: What should be different about your hood map compared to the one you have in mind?
answers.answer: Keep a hood/neighbourhood feel, but make it an original layout with different streets, buildings, and landmarks rather than copying a specific map.

answers.ask: How many blocks should the neighbourhood cover?
answers.answer: Use a small map covering about 4 city blocks so it is easy to play and build.

--- clarifications from the author ---
- [goal] What mode is this - team deathmatch, free-for-all, or an objective? Make it free-for-all so players spawn into the map and fight each other.
- [free] What should be different about your hood map compared to the one you have in mind? Keep a hood/neighbourhood feel, but make it an original layout with different streets, buildings, and landmarks rather than copying a specific map.
- [scale] How many blocks should the neighbourhood cover? Use a small map covering about 4 city blocks so it is easy to play and build.
config.genre_evidence: "Make An FPS Shooter Game" and "free-for-all so players spawn into the map and fight each other." The four-block neighbourhood map is built as a shared combat map for player-versus-player gunfights.

config.addendum:
LAYOUT FEATURES for this Shooter map. Build these as the actual structure of the space rather than as set dressing, keep them visually distinct from one another, and keep the whole layout legible in one view.

SHAPE OF THE SPACE - Lane Network: Parallel routes, classically three, channelling team traffic into predictable engagement fronts.

INCLUDE:
- Tactical Cover Arrays: Waist-high (3–4 studs) and full-body (7–8 studs) cover distributed evenly across every lane.
- Interconnected Rooms: Rooms with two or more entrances and exits, favouring constant interconnectedness over realistic dead ends.
- Settlement: Built-up ground at a stated density — a hamlet, a town, or a dense city block grid — rather than scattered individual buildings.
